This interlocutory application has been filed by the appellant, praying therein to suspend the
sentence and release him on bail during the pendency of this appeal.

2.  The appellant has been convicted under Sections 376(3) of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act in connection with Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 113 of 2020 arising out of Chirkunda (Panchet O.P.) P.S.
Case No. 215 of 2020.
He has been sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for twenty years and a fine of Rs. 10,000/- for the offence under Section 6 of POCSO Act.

3. Heard, the learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.
4.
Opportunity was given to the State to oppose the bail, which the State availed and opposed.

In her examination-in-chief, she states that since last four years,
they were in relationship on the pretext of marriage.
6. Considering the aforesaid facts and the fact that there is no likelihood of hearing of this appeal in near future, we are inclined to allow this interlocutory application.

Accordingly, upon suspending Vicky Bhuiyan @ Vicky Kumar @ Vicky ... vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65025366/
1 the sentence, the appellant, named above, is directed to be released on bail during the pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Special Judge-POCSO, Dhanbad in connection with Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 113 of 2020 arising out of Chirkunda (Panchet O.P.) P.S.
Case No. 215 of 2020 with a condition that the appellant shall appear and mark his attendance before the Registrar, Civil Court, Dhanbad once in every four months till the disposal of this appeal.
